title: Iterated blow-up conjecture for inducibility of directed paths
statement:
Let $\vec{P}_k$ be the directed path on $k$ vertices, and let $\vec{C}_{k+1}$ be the directed cycle on $k+1$ vertices. For an oriented graph $G$, write $d_{\vec{P}_k}(G)$ for the induced density of $\vec{P}_k$, and let $I(\vec{P}_k)$ be the limiting maximum of this density over all oriented graphs. An iterated balanced blow-up of $\vec{C}_{k+1}$ is obtained by repeatedly replacing each vertex by equally sized independent classes and orienting edges between classes according to the directed cycle.

**Iterated blow-up conjecture.** The number of induced copies of $\vec{P}_k$ over all oriented graphs on $n$ vertices is maximized by an iterated balanced blow-up of $\vec{C}_{k+1}$. Consequently,

$$
I(\vec{P}_k)=\frac{k!}{(k+1)^{k-1}-1}.
$$

The conjecture extends the announced result $I(\vec{P}_3)=2/5$ with extremal construction an iterated blow-up of $\vec{C}_4$. It is presented as an open generalization for longer oriented paths.
source_name: Ilkyoo Choi, Bernard Lidický and Florian Pfender, “Inducibility of directed paths”, arXiv:1811.03747 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.03747

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2018). “This is still an open question for almost all values of $k$.”
